content.text: {"decision":"NO","supporting_policy_ids":["E08","E10","E06"],"missing_facts":[],"justification":"The £260 payment from Robyn Ellis cannot qualify for Gift Aid. Policy passage E10 explicitly excludes donations 'that are a payment for goods or services or made because your charity or CASC bought goods and services.' The evidence clearly shows the £260 was a payment for advertising services (placement in the newsletter and on the website), confirmed by the January emails and the subsequent delivery of the advertisement. The label 'donation' in the bookkeeping sheet does not change the nature of the transaction. Because this exclusion applies conclusively, there is no need to assess Robyn's tax position or Gift Aid declaration for this payment. Regarding the separate £20 cash gift in December: the policy passages E04/E05/E07 require the donor to have paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax as the Gift Aid claimed, and to have made a Gift Aid declaration. Neither Robyn's tax position nor whether she made a declaration for the £20 gift has been confirmed, so eligibility for Gift Aid on that separate £20 gift cannot be determined without more information. The question as posed focuses on Robyn Ellis's £260 payment, which is definitively excluded.","scope_issues":["The £20 December cash gift is a separate transaction; its Gift Aid eligibility is unresolved due to missing tax status and declaration information for Robyn Ellis."],"conditional_branches":[]}
